purpose: Original examples for contextual editorial review. These patterns support judgement; they are not automatic truth checks or AI-authorship signals.

local.title: Geekist project-language review
local.application: Project meanings, source constraints and bounded next actions govern each revision.

humanizer.title: Humanizer v3.1.0
humanizer.application: Concrete editing examples, factual checks and contextual exceptions inform the presentation.

plain-language-editor.title: Plain Language Editor
plain-language-editor.application: Stable pattern identifiers and checks for meaning, claims and sentence relationships inform the organisation. No upstream catalogue is copied.

patterns.name: Changed project meaning
patterns.source_facts: Reviewed means all document checks are complete. Approval is a separate decision that has not been made.
patterns.after: All document checks are complete. An approval decision is still pending.
patterns.reason: Restore the distinction between completed checks and approval rather than polishing the wrong state.
patterns.exception: Keep an approved label when the governing source records an approval decision. Different audience labels are acceptable when their meanings agree.

patterns.name: Lost condition
patterns.source_facts: Only workspace owners can export selected notes. The supported format is Markdown.
patterns.before: Anyone can export all notes in any format.
patterns.after: Workspace owners can export selected notes as Markdown.
patterns.reason: Retain the actor, selection boundary and supported format that change what the reader may do.
patterns.exception: A short label may omit detail when the adjacent explanation makes the relevant conditions clear. Do not remove a condition that changes a user's decision.

patterns.name: Invented result
patterns.source_facts: Six internal participants gave feedback on the export flow. The trial did not measure time savings.
patterns.before: Our trial proved that export cuts reporting time in half.
patterns.after: Six internal participants gave feedback on the export flow.
patterns.reason: Describe the observed result and leave the unsupported time-saving claim out. Record the measurement needed if that stronger claim matters.
patterns.exception: Retain a quantified benefit when a relevant measurement supports it, including the population and conditions needed to interpret the figure.

patterns.name: Evidence gap becomes a blanket stop
patterns.source_facts: A reversible local adapter prototype and local tests are authorised. Real-client behaviour has not been checked. No external deployment is authorised.
patterns.before: Compatibility is unproven, so stop all implementation.
patterns.after: Build the authorised local prototype and run local tests. Check real-client behaviour before claiming compatibility. Keep external deployment outside this work.
patterns.reason: Separate the missing compatibility evidence from the work already authorised and preserve the actual external-action boundary.
patterns.exception: Keep a stop instruction when a demonstrated incompatibility, required input, permission boundary or explicit user instruction blocks that named action.

patterns.name: Data structure becomes prose
patterns.source_facts: An invited reviewer can view a report until 14 November. The reviewer cannot edit it.
patterns.before: The report object has a reviewer-scoped read-only access grant with a 14 November expiry attribute.
patterns.after: The invited reviewer can view this report until 14 November, but cannot edit it.
patterns.reason: Explain the actor, action and limit rather than making the reader reconstruct a permission record.
patterns.exception: Keep exact field names and values in API or schema reference material. Explain their consequences alongside the contract instead of renaming identifiers.

patterns.name: Commentary hides the finding
patterns.source_facts: The import stopped because the supplied file has no header row. The user must add the row before retrying.
patterns.before: It is important to note the following key finding: the import failed due to an issue with the header.
patterns.after: The import stopped because the file has no header row. Add the header row and retry.
patterns.reason: Lead with the observed failure and useful next action, replacing vague commentary with the actual cause.
patterns.exception: Keep navigation instructions when they help the reader use a long guide or choose a relevant section. Not every sentence about the document is redundant.

patterns.name: Necessary context is missing
patterns.source_facts: A queue for each project keeps its scheduling separate. The intended audience includes readers unfamiliar with queues.
patterns.before: The per-project queue resolves the scheduling issue.
patterns.after: Each project has its own waiting list of jobs, called a queue, so its scheduling stays separate from other projects.
patterns.reason: Introduce the necessary term and explain the consequence without promising an unmeasured performance improvement.
patterns.exception: Use the accepted specialist term directly when the intended reader already knows it or can reach its definition. Do not expand every familiar abbreviation on every page.

patterns.name: Editing flattens the author's voice
patterns.source_facts: The author is writing a lightly witty personal essay about repeatedly losing draft notes. No product performance claim is being made.
patterns.before: The author experienced repeated difficulties with draft-note retention.
patterns.after: I kept losing my draft notes. Apparently, I was running a disappearing-ink experiment.
patterns.reason: Use the author's stated register while preserving the event. The second sentence is an obvious humorous aside, not a technical claim.
patterns.exception: Keep neutral wording in a technical reference or when humour would obscure a consequential condition. Preserve uncertainty and personal detail when they carry meaning.
